requirement.part: cantilever bracket, load at the tip

brief:
Part: cantilever bracket, load at the tip. Solid rectangular cross-section, width across the load, thickness in the load direction.
Load 600 N at the tip, length 150 mm.
REQ-001 yield margin of safety >= 0 with factor 1.25 (MS = allowable / (factor x stress) - 1).
REQ-002 ultimate margin of safety >= 0 with factor 1.4.
REQ-003 tip deflection <= 1.5 mm.
REQ-004 width 20-80 mm, thickness 3-8 mm.
REQ-005 thickness must be a stock plate thickness: [3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 25, 30] mm.
REQ-006 REQ-001 to REQ-003 must still hold with the load 10% higher and the plate 0.5 mm thinner.
REQ-007 thickness / width <= 2 (a proxy for lateral stability).
Materials: {"Al 6061-T6": {"density_kg_m3": 2700, "youngs_modulus_gpa": 68.9, "yield_mpa": 276.0, "ultimate_mpa": 310.0}, "Ti-6Al-4V": {"density_kg_m3": 4430, "youngs_modulus_gpa": 113.8, "yield_mpa": 880.0, "ultimate_mpa": 950.0}, "Steel 4130": {"density_kg_m3": 7850, "youngs_modulus_gpa": 205.0, "yield_mpa": 435.0, "ultimate_mpa": 670.0}}
Goal: the lowest mass that meets every requirement.

reasoning:
Cantilever with tip load P=600 N, L=150 mm. Rectangular section width b (20-80 mm), thickness t (3-8 mm, stock sizes only from list: 3,4,5,6,8). Governing checks: bending stress sigma = 6PL/(b t^2). Yield MS with factor 1.25: sigma <= 276/1.25 = 220.8 MPa for Al; Ti: 880/1.25 = 704 MPa; Steel: 435/1.25 = 348 MPa. Ultimate with factor 1.4 gives tighter for Al: 310/1.4=221.4 MPa, steel 670/1.4=478.6, Ti 950/1.4=678.6. Stiffness: delta = PL^3/(3EI) = 4PL^3/(E b t^3) <= 1.5 mm. Robustness case (REQ-006): P=660 N, t reduced by 0.5 mm, so t-0.5 must be a stock size or the check is done on the physical thickness; the worst case is t_min = t-0.5 with 1.1P. Note REQ-005 restricts t to stock values, so t=6 gives 5.5 under the check; t=8 gives 7.5; t=5 gives 4.5. Mass proportional to density*b*t. Also REQ-007: t/b <= 2 so b >= t/2, and b>=20 is the binding constraint for small t.
Note for Al: yield-governed by 1.25 factor is not the limit; ultimate factor 1.4 gives allowable 221.4 MPa, bending stress with t=6, b=20: 6*600*150/(20*36)=540000/720=750 MPa — too high. Need b t^2 >= 6PL/allow. For Al with 1.1P,t-0.5: 6*660*150/(221.4)=2.68e6/221.4... compute: 6*660*150=594000 N·mm; divided by 221 MPa gives b*t_eff^2 >= 2686 mm^3. Deflection: 4*660*150^3/(68900*b*t_eff^3)<=1.5 gives b*t_eff^3 >= 4*660*3.375e6/(68900*1.5)=8.91e9/103350≈86200 mm^4... so need b*t_eff^3 >= ~86,000 (units mm^4 with E in MPa). Those tell the search region: Al needs thicker/wider sections; steel and Ti are stiffness-limited differently. Let me just give notes.
Ti: E=113.8 GPa, deflection needs b*t_eff^3 >= 86200*68.9/113.8 ≈ 52,200; strength allowable ~678 MPa so b t_eff^2 >= 594000/678 ≈ 876. Stiffness governs.
Steel: E=205 GPa, deflection b t_eff^3 >= 86200*68.9/205 ≈ 28,970; strength allowable 348 MPa (yield with 1.25) → b t_eff^2 >= 594000/348 ≈ 1707. Strength governs-ish.
Mass per length ∝ density*b*t. Al density 2700 is lowest, but Al needs most section for stiffness-limited... Let's just assign notes to specialists and let them search; the function requires assignments with notes.

notes.Al 6061-T6: Search b=20-80 mm and t=5-8 mm (stock 5, 6, 8); stiffness is the binding limit, needing roughly b*t_eff^3 >= 8.6e4 mm^4 with t_eff = t-0.5 for REQ-006, and the 1.4 ultimate factor caps bending stress near 221 MPa. Mass is lowest per unit volume (2700 kg/m3), so this is the likely winner if a feasible section exists.
notes.Ti-6Al-4V: Search t=4-6 mm and b=20-40 mm; with E=113.8 GPa the deflection limit needs b*t_eff^3 >= ~5.2e4 mm^4 and strength is easily met (allowable ~678 MPa). Density 4430 kg/m3 means it only wins if it allows a much thinner section than Al.
notes.Steel 4130: Search t=3-5 mm and narrow b=20-35 mm where mass stays low; stiffness needs b*t_eff^3 >= ~2.9e4 mm^4 (E=205 GPa) and yield at 1.25 caps stress at 348 MPa, needing b*t_eff^2 >= ~1700 mm^3. Density 7850 kg/m3 penalizes it, so only thin sections are worth checking.

text: I'll start by checking the largest sections the limits allow, since stiffness looks like the binding constraint.
I'll start by checking three candidates that span the feasible range: the largest allowed section, a mid-size one, and a thinner one.

I'll check a few candidates first. My hand calculation says the REQ-006 stiffness case (load 660 N, plate 7.5 mm) is the binding constraint. That needs roughly b ≥ 69 mm at t = 8 mm, and no thinner plate can meet it within the 80 mm width limit.

The first three checks show that deflection is the binding constraint, and the formula explains it. Deflection scales as 1/(b·t³), and the largest section allowed by REQ-004 is 80 × 8 mm, which still gives 1.74 mm. I'll check a few more points to confirm there is no feasible region inside the envelope.
The 69 × 8 mm design passes, and the 30 × 8 and 35 × 5 designs fail. I'll check a few more widths at 8 mm to bracket the lightest passing design and fill out the proposal set.

The lightest passing Steel 4130 design is 69 × 8 mm at about 650 g. Thickness is capped at 8 mm by REQ-004, and the REQ-006 stiffness case forces the width to about 69 mm. I used 7 of the 10 checks allowed.

Four proposals, all checked with `check_design` and all passing every requirement:

| # | Width × thickness (mm) | Yield MS (nominal) | Tip deflection (nominal, mm) | Mass (g) | REQ-006 worst

**No Al 6061-T6 design can meet every requirement.** Tip stiffness is the binding limit, and it cannot be met inside the REQ-004 envelope (width 20–80 mm, thickness 3–8 mm). I checked the three largest sections and the closed-form beam formulas reproduce the tool exactly, so I did not spend more checks on smaller sections.

**Why it's infeasible:** Nominal tip deflection is δ = PL³/(3EI) = 9798/I

No Ti-6Al-4V design inside the stated envelope meets all requirements. Tip deflection is the binding constraint, not strength. Every candidate I checked has large strength margins but fails REQ-003 (≤1.5 mm), and therefore also fails REQ-006.

Why it can't close: deflection = 71,180 / (b·t³) mm, so REQ-003 needs b·t³ ≥ 47,453 mm⁴. The largest section allowed by REQ-004 (80 × 8 mm) gives b·t³ = 40,

items.title: Factors of safety
items.detail: Yield 1.25 and ultimate 1.4 are illustrative. Confirm them against the program's structural standard and its test approach.

items.title: Material allowables
items.detail: The analysis uses typical handbook values. Flight hardware needs statistically based allowables for this alloy, temper and thickness.

items.title: Material specification
items.detail: Call out AMS 6350 (normalized plate) on the drawing.

items.title: Specialty metals (DoD work)
items.detail: Steel 4130 is a specialty metal: for DoD work the melt must come from the US or a qualifying country. Ask the vendor for melt-source certification.

items.title: Material traceability
items.detail: Require a certificate of conformance and mill test report traceable to the heat lot.

items.title: Supplier quality
items.detail: Prefer machine shops with an aerospace quality system. See Vendors.
